lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Rebuilt weekly carrier scorecards used by 6 regional managers to renegotiate contracts, cutting late deliveries from 11% to 7% in two quarters.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The current Coastal Marine Services entry dominates the first impression without supporting the résumé’s product direction.
items.because: Its content does not connect to the MBA, internship, and projects that tell the product story.

items.says: Experience is not listed newest-first.
items.because: The 2018–2023 Crestline role appears above the 2024 Harbor Payments internship.

items.says: The five-day turnaround has no comparison point.
The inspection-related maintenance bullet gives no result.
items.because: It does not say whether the work kept the winches reliable, resolved issues, or supported a successful inspection.

items.says: The maintenance description does not say what work you performed.
The 30% reduction has no baseline, follow-up rates, or measurement period.
Passive phrasing hides who implemented the redesign.
The bullet uses a first-person pronoun.
The route-planning result is buried after a long list of methods.
items.because: A reader scanning the tasks may miss the 1,800-hour saving.

items.says: The checkout lift is reported before the testing and rollout details.
items.because: The review says the placement makes the rollout easy to miss.

items.says: Conventional RICE Reach is not the number of support tickets a feature would close.
items.because: Reach estimates the number of people or users affected over a defined period.

items.says: The bullet names the RICE process but not the priority or decision it produced.
items.because: Without the outcome, the significance of the prioritization is hard to assess.

items.says: The explanation of the Reach metric is wordy.
The loss analysis gives no estimate of the loss.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the scale that supported the roadmap decision.

items.says: The roadmap priority is not named.
items.because: The wording does not identify what was selected, making the product impact difficult to picture.

items.says: The roadmap outcome comes after a long list of process steps.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the decision that gives those steps their purpose.

items.says: The checkout lift is reported as a customer-level effect even though the test randomized by session.
items.because: Session randomization estimates a session-level effect unless the analysis accounted for repeated sessions or each customer contributed only once.

items.says: The test-detail bullet repeats the checkout lift already reported in the preceding bullet.
items.because: Repeating the result takes space from other evidence about your work.

items.says: The unit of the five-point conversion change is unspecified.
items.because: Percentage points and relative percent describe different-sized effects.

items.says: The leadership team’s funding decision is buried in a relative clause.
The onboarding and checkout results sit apart from the remaining roadmap bullets.
The launch result does not explain your product-lead contribution.
items.because: It shows the project’s impact but not what you personally owned or how you helped deliver it.

items.says: The relationship between the 3,100 students and two dining halls is unclear.
The food description uses a wordy passive phrase.
The weekly-active-user increase is 187.5%, not 150%.
items.because: The increase of 750 users is 187.5% of the starting value of 400.

items.says: The bullet does not say who chose the reminders or how interviews informed the choice.
The fill-rate change is 20 percentage points, not 20%.
items.because: From 75% to 95% is a 20-percentage-point change, or about a 26.7% relative increase.

items.says: The bullet does not explain how the volunteer shifts improved slot fill.
items.because: A reader cannot connect the volunteer system to the result.

items.says: The client-funded pilot comes after the savings estimate and is easy to miss.
items.because: The pilot is the concrete outcome, but a scanning reader may overlook the client’s decision.

items.says: The savings model does not say what informed it.
The shortened form has no measure of the change or its effect.
items.because: Adoption does not show whether intake became meaningfully faster or simpler.

items.says: Passive phrasing hides your actions on the intake work.
The intake-form work reads as a separate strand from the scheduling recommendation.
The recommendation is presented, but the analysis behind it is not described.
items.because: The work behind the pilot approval remains unclear.

items.says: “Final” is filler.
